answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent to one work history: every task writes a signed receipt into a public ledger tied to a single persistent identity, and reputation decays when the agent goes idle. New identities start at zero trust and earn it slowly through real work, while splitting effort across many fake identities dilutes each one's score. Like timber cut from one meadow, reputation cannot be cloned, it must grow in place, and a bridge of audited receipts links past performance to future access, so an attacker pays in time and real output, not cheap new accounts.
